candidate_name: EA Energy Wilson City LNG-to-Power Facility (Abaco)
sponsor_or_proposer: EA Energy Limited (JV of Verdant Limited and Consus Energy)
current_state: Construction. PPA signed with GoB April 2025; environmental approvals secured and financing finalized; site-clearing/groundbreaking reported Aug 2025; commissioning targeted Q3/Q4 2026. Site adjacent to BPL Wilson City power plant, Abaco. 30 MWe gas engines + 15 MWp solar + 15 MWh BESS. Per EA Energy: 'Both Power Plants will also include Regasification and Storage Facilities capable of processing and storing LNG'; LNG delivered by sea then road in ISO containers into on-site storage tanks.
missing_threshold_elements: None for the §3 add bar (sponsor + location + concrete step all present). Held in monitor pending a GEM SCOPE decision: is a small (~30 MWe) ISO-container-fed mini-regas + storage skid feeding island gas engines a trackable LNG import/regasification terminal, or power-plant fuel infrastructure outside the terminals tracker? Comparable in scale to GEM's existing Island Power Producers (Nassau Mini LNG) row, which argues for inclusion.
watch_for: Commissioning / first LNG receipt; whether GEM methodology team confirms small islanded regas+storage skids are in-scope as terminals; capacity in MTPA/regas terms (only MWe power capacity is public).
notes: Verified URLs (url_verifier PASS): https://eaenergybahamas.com/ ; https://ewnews.com/ea-energy-breaks-ground-on-hybrid-power-plants-to-end-abaco-and-eleuthera-outages-by-2026/ ; https://ewnews.com/government-signs-power-purchase-agreements-to-transform-energy-sector-in-abaco-eleuthera-exumas-and-new-providence/ . Not in GEM (grep + entity_lookup confirm EA Energy/Verdant/Consus absent). If GEM confirms in-scope, stage as a new_terminal (import, status=construction) with Owner=EA Energy Limited, Parent=Verdant Limited; Consus Energy; Location=Wilson City, Abaco.

candidate_name: EA Energy Hatchet Bay LNG-to-Power Facility (Eleuthera)
sponsor_or_proposer: EA Energy Limited (JV of Verdant Limited and Consus Energy)
current_state: Construction. Same PPA package (April 2025) and Aug 2025 groundbreaking/site-clearing as the Abaco facility; environmental approvals secured, financing finalized; commissioning Q3/Q4 2026. Site adjacent to BPL Hatchet Bay Power Station, Eleuthera. ~14.7-20 MWe gas engines + 10 MWp solar + 10 MWh BESS. Includes on-site LNG regasification and storage facilities; LNG delivered by sea then road in ISO containers.
missing_threshold_elements: None for the §3 add bar. Held in monitor for the same GEM SCOPE question as the Abaco sibling (ISO-container-fed mini-regas + storage feeding island gas engines).
watch_for: Commissioning / first LNG receipt; GEM scope confirmation; regas/storage capacity figures (only MWe power capacity public; sources vary 14.7 vs 20 MWe).
notes: Verified URLs as above (url_verifier PASS). Same sponsor and likely same single entity_addition as the Abaco facility. Two physically distinct sites (Abaco vs Eleuthera) under one developer; would be two GEM terminals if staged.

sponsor_or_proposer: Exuma Renewable Energy Corporation (FONSIS + Bahamian investors, ~62.5% Bahamian; director Philip Whitehead)
current_state: Proposed/early construction. PPA signed with GoB April 2025; part of the same Abaco/Eleuthera/Exuma energy-transformation package; construction stated to begin Q3 2025, completion Q3 2026. Location Georgetown, Exuma. 8.5 MWe LNG generation + 3 MWp solar + 6 MWh BESS. Described as an 'LNG generation facility'; on-site LNG receiving/regas not independently confirmed at primary-source level (lighter sourcing than the EA Energy sites).
missing_threshold_elements: Concrete step is present (signed PPA) but the LNG receiving/regasification component is less clearly documented than the EA Energy sites; no developer primary source confirming on-site regas + storage found this sweep. Same GEM SCOPE question applies, plus weaker terminal-component evidence.
watch_for: Independent confirmation that the Georgetown plant has an on-site LNG receiving/regas + storage facility (vs purely a gas engine fueled from trucked CNG/LNG); groundbreaking; GEM scope confirmation.
notes: Verified URL (url_verifier PASS): the ewnews PPA-signing article. Not in GEM. Smallest of the three (8.5 MWe); most likely to fall below any terminal-tracking scope bar. Different developer (Exuma Renewable Energy Corp) from the EA Energy sites.
